column1: SECTION 1: HOW TO USE AND UNDERSTAND THE VIN

column2: A Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) is a unique code assigned to every motor vehicle when it's manufactured. It can be decoded to reveal the Month and Year of production.

The VIN is usually a 17-character string (sometimes up to 20 for specific brands like Hyundai/Fiat in India) stamped in the engine bay, around the passenger compartment, or on a placard near the front doors.

1. Find your vehicle's VIN. 2. Locate your car's manufacturer in Section 2 to find which character positions correspond to the Month and Year. 3. Match those specific characters with the Month and Year Code tables in Sections 3 and 4.
Always count the characters from left to right.

column1: SECTION 2: MANUFACTURER VIN DECODING RULES (ALL 18 BRANDS)

column4: Look for a separate placard near the front left door (bottom right) for a 2-character Month/Year code (e.g., GF = July 2015).
10th Digit is Year (e.g., 2=2001, 3=2002); 11th is Plant Code; 12th is Month.
VIN string may be 19 characters long.
e.g., NZ = 2010. String is longer than the standard 17 characters.
10th character represents the MODEL YEAR. 5th/6th together make the calendar year (e.g., 12 = 2012).
Toyota VINs often do not encode the month directly; check seatbelt tags or factory placards for exact month.
Follows standard ISO 3779 for 10th character year.
